regions.merged_text: As for yourself dear Sister Agnes Carmel; since I read the first half dozen pages of your big letter, I have been convinced that there is nothing wrong with your mind atall. It has seemed to me that you have been suffering for someone else - most likely for just your same dear Parents and folks, and of course at the sametime for your humiliation and con-sequently your purification. You really ought to thank God for offering you such a mission. I might rather say for imposing it on you; for other- wise you woul hardly have had the courage to consent to it. I mean to the sacrifice it has cost you. And the victory (over the devil and scandal), is not as yet gained. At the time of your last letter, when you requested the return of said long letter, I did not really know where I had put it and consequently had to let go. Just a few days ago I came across it and I decided again to write to your Father and see if possibly I can do somthing to promote peace in his poor soul and in his family; for I am sure that after these long years of estrangement from the Church, from the Holy Sacraments and from religion which alone promotes peace that the world can not give, He must be longing for a change of some kind. I have no doubt God will have mercy on him and help us. For I believe he has a heart that wants to do right. I thought, therefore, dear Sister Agnes Carmel that before I would write him, I would ask you about any change that possibly has come to your Father since you wrote me about him. This es- pecially sinc it is so long that I have not heard from you - and about him, And otherwise too the outlook may have changed. Besides; if you have any suggestions to make as to the way I might approach him, etc, I would certainly be glad to receive them. Furthermore, if you still
